name: How much does a bathroom remodel usually cost in Los Angeles, and what’s a fair price for a small vs. large bathroom?

mainEntity.name: How much does a bathroom remodel usually cost in Los Angeles, and what’s a fair price for a small vs. large bathroom?

acceptedAnswer.text:
In Los Angeles County, many small to mid-size bathroom remodels range roughly from $20,000–$50,000+, while larger or primary suites can go from $40,000–$90,000+ depending on finishes and complexity. A basic pull-and-replace is on the low end; full gut and luxury finishes push higher. 
Context: Bathrooms are expensive per square foot because of plumbing, waterproofing, tile work, and ventilation requirements. Older homes often need upgrades to plumbing lines, electrical circuits, and framing once walls are opened. 
Key factors:
- Size and whether you’re moving fixtures or adding a shower/tub
- Tile type and coverage area (floor-to-ceiling tile costs more)
- Plumbing/electrical upgrades and waterproofing requirements
- Custom vs prefabricated vanities, glass, and fixtures
Practical guidance: Decide early whether you want a basic refresh or a full gut, then get multiple written bids using the same scope. Ask how much of the budget is labor vs materials and what’s included in waterproofing and inspections. Soft positioning: A knowledgeable remodeler will help you tailor the design to your target budget while meeting code and durability needs.
acceptedAnswer.description: In Los Angeles, smaller bathrooms often run around $20,000–$50,000+, while larger or primary baths can be $40,000–$90,000+ depending on layout changes, tile, and finishes. Clearly define whether you’re doing a basic refresh or a full gut and get detailed, apples-to-apples bids so you know what a fair price looks like.
